title: Windowed Batch Concurrency Explorer (scratch)
summary: Exploratory scratchpad for windowed-batching + concurrency sizing heuristics. Focus: quick cost vs p95 tradeoffs, simple queueing approximations, spreadsheet-driven sensitivity runs.
body:
Context
------
Quick playground doc to capture intuition, cheap closed-form approximations, and a short sim plan for windowed (time-slotted) batching combined with concurrency caps. This is intentionally lightweight — think notes-to-self + equations to drop into the shared spreadsheet.

Goal
----
- Produce a small set of sizing heuristics (rules-of-thumb) for: batch window W, per-GPU concurrency cap C, and reserve headroom H to hit a target p95 latency.
- Generate spreadsheet scenarios for common arrival shapes (steady, diurnal, microburst).
- Estimate unit cost (USD / 1M generated tokens) under each scenario.

Definitions & assumptions (baseline)
---------------------------------
- Arrival process: approx Poisson with mean rate lambda (reqs/sec). We'll test lambda in {10, 50, 200, 800} (per-route baseline).
- Prompt length (tokens_in): 32 (median), generation length (tokens_out): 64 (median). Total tokens = 96.
- Model perf (single GPU): base single-request per-token effective throughput approximated as S = 1200 tokens/sec at batch=1 (low parallelism). Large batches improve tokens/sec sublinearly due to kernel overhead: T(b) = S * (1 + 0.012 * (b-1)) up to saturate. (Rough empirical fit for our 70B quantized variant)
- Inference latency per request depends on batch composition: L_service(b) = (tokens_total / T(b)) + L_fixed where L_fixed = 6 ms (dispatch / networking overhead).
- Windowed batching: server holds incoming requests for up to W ms to collect a batch; on expiry or when batch_size == B_max we dispatch. Waiting adds tail-sensitive queuing delay.
- Concurrency cap C: number of simultaneous in-flight batches/GPU or across N GPUs (we size per-GPU and then scale horizontally).
- Cache/KV hit: prefix cache hit rate h = 0.15 (saves 30% tokens on average). We'll parameterize h in spreadsheet.

Latency decomposition (simple)
----------------------------
Observed latency (per request) = wait_time + service_time + network_overhead.
Approx rules:
- avg_wait ≈ W/2 for uniformly arriving requests inside the window (but increases with lambda and early dispatch triggers).
- p95_wait ≈ min(W, 3*(avg_wait)) as a conservative tail fudge. (This is a heuristic to avoid full queuing math in the quick model.)
- service_time approximated by L_service where batch size is expected batch occupancy b_eff = min(B_max, lambda * W + burst_factor).

Example arithmetic (baseline numbers)
------------------------------------
Baseline: lambda = 200 req/s, W = 15 ms (0.015 s), B_max = 16.
- expected arrivals per window = lambda * W = 200 * 0.015 = 3 requests -> b_eff ≈ 3 (so small batch)
- T(b=3) = 1200 * (1 + 0.012*2) ≈ 1200 * 1.024 = 1228.8 tokens/s
- tokens_total = 96 -> service_time ≈ 96 / 1228.8 ≈ 0.078s = 78 ms
- avg_wait ≈ 7.5 ms, p95_wait heuristic ≈ min(15 ms, 3*7.5 = 22.5 ms) -> 15 ms (window bound)
- total p95 ≈ 15 + 78 + 6 = 99 ms -> comfortably under 150 ms p95 target

Observations: small windows keep wait low but also keep batch sizes small -> higher tokens/sec per token but limited batching benefits. For high lambda, windows accumulate larger batches and throughput improves.

Sizing heuristics (first-draft)
-------------------------------
- Target p95 budget (T_budget) = 150 ms. Reserve 20% for network/other (N_headroom = 0.2 * T_budget). So inference+wait budget ~ 120 ms.
- Choose W such that for median load lambda_med, expected service_time(lambda_med, W) + W <= inference+wait budget. Use conservative p95_wait = W for tail.
- Concurrency cap C per GPU: choose C = ceil( (lambda_peak * E[service_time]) / per_gpu_throughput_factor ), where per_gpu_throughput_factor is the average number of concurrent batches a GPU can handle given kernel-level parallelism. Start with per_gpu_throughput_factor = 1 for simplicity (one batch occupies GPU).
- Headroom H: multiply C by 1.2 (20% capacity buffer) to absorb short microbursts without scaling.

Cost proxies
------------
- We convert concurrency to number of GPUs needed: GPUs = ceil( lambda * E[service_time] / (1 - preemption_factor) / (GPU_util_per_batch) ). For first-pass use: GPUs ≈ ceil( (lambda * tokens_total) / (GPU_tokens_per_sec_peak * average_concurrency_effectiveness) ).
- Unit cost = GPUs * cost_per_GPU_hour / (throughput_tokens_per_hour) -> compute USD / 1M tokens. Spreadsheet contains actual cost numbers by instance type.

Microburst behavior and guardrails
----------------------------------
- For short microbursts (duration < W), windowing actually helps by absorbing the burst into larger batches and improving tokens/sec, but p95_wait can spike to W (the worst-case).
- For sustained microbursts, concurrency will grow and scale triggers must be tuned. Prefer canary-scale-up thresholds that include both queue depth and service_time percentiles.
- Suggest two operating modes: "latency-first" (W <= 10ms, H small) and "cost-first" (W up to 50ms, larger headroom, pack more).

Spreadsheet plan (columns)
-------------------------
- scenario_name, lambda, burst_shape (steady|short_burst|sustained_burst|diurnal_peak), W_ms, B_max, cache_hit, model_variant, tokens_total, T(b) formula used, b_eff, avg_wait_ms, p95_wait_ms, service_ms, total_p95_ms, GPUs_needed, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, notes

Sim plan (short)
----------------
- Implement an event-driven simulator (spreadsheet or small python in repo) to validate heuristics across: lambda in [10,50,200,800], W in [5,15,30,50], burst_factor in [1,2,5,10], B_max in [8,16,32].
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, average token throughput, GPU occupancy curve, queue length distribution.
- Compare closed-form heuristic to sim results and compute correction factors.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- How to fold KV cache semantics into service_time properly? (cache hits change tokens_total and may alter batching composition because cached prefixes can be served faster). Need a simple model: tokens_total = tokens_in*(1 - h) + tokens_out. But if cached prefixes short-circuit KV compute path, service shape changes nonlinearly. TODO: ask applied-ml for microbench numbers.
- Our T(b) fit is toy; need real kernel-level profs for small b (1..8) and medium b (8..48). Diego to share perf-ci traces (GH PR linked above).
- Validation: run the spreadsheet against synthetic replay of real production traces for one small customer route (anonymized) to calibrate burst_factor.
- Where to encode dynamic fallback? If p95 drift > threshold, route should fallback to faster model variant (smaller tokens_out or quantized variant). Need to model fallback latency penalty and cost delta.

Quick action items
------------------
- [ ] Fill spreadsheet with the baseline model perf numbers (Ava) -> linked spreadsheet.
- [ ] Small python sim for two routes (Priya) to validate heuristics for short bursts.
- [ ] Get kernel perf curves for b=1..64 (Diego) and update T(b) model.
- [ ] Draft one-pager with recommended W/C/H defaults for customer onboarding (target: internal runtime runbook).

Notes-to-self (informal)
-----------------------
- If lambda * W << 1 (<< 1 arrival per window), batching not useful; prefer micro-batching or no-window mode.
- There's tension between window size and jitter: larger windows help pack but increase tail and make CPU work (prefetch, kernel warm-up) less predictable.
- Possible hybrid: start with W_small for initial p95 target and allow queue depth to trigger short wait extension if system is underutilized ("aggressive pack when idle"). This is promising but increases implementation complexity; treat as v2.

References
----------
- perf traces: GH PR 342 (linked), spreadsheet 'windowed-batch-sim' (linked).
- Related internal notes: see serving-runtime/burst-affinity-cost-model-playbook-wip.json and microburst-reservoir-batching-explainer-wip.json for prior thinking (overlap intentionally small).

End of scratchpad
-----------------
I'll iterate this into the shared spreadsheet and move key heuristics to the playbook once we have sim -> heuristic correction factors.
